title: Imitators and rival bands, and his attack on jazz critics
summary: He names northern bands that copied the ODJB, insists none changed the rhythm, and says only newspapers, not handbills, are proof.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Who is Red Brown? Tom Brown

Tom Brown That's what they call him, Red Brown That's what I know about They came back They may have went to Chicago And they broke up with other bands We were still packing them in It's a funny thing that the northern men who began copying the music from the Dixieland Jazz Band was to make good You had Ted Lewis, I don't say he played good jazz I don't say he ever played jazz But they were trying to copy You had Earl Fuller You had Ross Garland You had Vince Lopez The Memphis Five The Indiana Five All people from the north You had the Darcy brothers With the Clam Big Seven And they clad the jazz band in 1919 That's what they first played jazz The Memphis Five they played They copied from the records of the Dixieland Jazz Band And if anyone wants to go listen to their recordings And the other records All of them copied Now as well as I had talents of changing things around I believe these other men who followed us must have had a certain gift of talent That they could take these licks and make them sound a little different But now when it comes down to rhythm No one has ever improved on it Or no one has ever been able to get away from the rhythm They may have changed the licks But they never have changed that rhythm That was started by the Dixieland Jazz Band And of the thousands of places who was crying for this kind of music That the New Orleans boys was staying in the background is beyond me Only with the coming of the jazz clubs That they needed a few Judas Iscariots to lie for them So they could turn around and give credit to the Negro race For something that they didn't have nothing to do in the beginning In the records that I show you Boy, we'll bear that out Because if it is said that these Negroes went before us Or Brown went before us And he played the same rhythm that I played And the same music that I played Then to them would have been the glory You would have never heard of Nick LaRocca Or either of the original Dixieland Jazz Band This day you would have heard of them But they made no impression And I say their music was no different than the music that was played By the other men from the north or the south Or the west or anywhere else It only was in one band And that was in the original Dixieland Jazz Band That takes a lot of ground But let them prove to me where they worked Any place that they worked that they made a success It's easy to have a handbill printed It's easy to make up your own stories and have people printed But it's not easy to have it put in paper which you did In the newspapers That's what I go by I don't go by hearsay I don't go by what's printed by these jazz clubs and these jazz critics I go by what is proof Like when you went to a court A court don't take hearsay and they don't take printing handbills Or made up handbills After 30 years these men begin to find out They dig up cops and different things to find where this music come from They'll look back on the recordings Now no one stopped these men from making records The criminal band said they could have made a record Well they may call me a liar But if Mr. King is still living and the Victor Company will verify What I tell you they made a record and it was not commercial It never was put out it was scrapped The same way that the Columbia Company did when they recorded us It was beyond their comparable comprehension They beat hammers they did all kinds of noise They wouldn't give us a chance to record And they ran us out the office We recorded for Columbia first Before we went the Victor What come to us The Victor come to us after we were a tremendous hit on Broadway Well we crowded the people in at every floor and brought And the rise of whatever was packed with people And we would build on the outside Home to the length of the name Original Dixaland Jazz Band They put just creators of jazz In electric sign And that stayed there for three years For three winters not three years We played in 17, 18, in the part of 19 A feat that has been unequaled by any musical organization or act to this day I believe I told you the change of Nunes being changed in Shields Now that's the second change in the band After Rides & Wevers In conjunction with Rides & Wevers We played shows around New York Which you will find notices In the Tulane Files I forgot to tell you we played show in Chicago With a fellow named Johnny Fogarty While we were at the casino gardens You'll find that in the Tulane Files too This was the first introduction of jazz into theaters
